sources: rules/ARCHITECTURE.md layer rule: domain imports nothing outside domain; application imports domain and ports; adapters implement ports; only the composition root wires adapters

decoys.why_not_a_defect: The composition root is the only module allowed to import an adapter. Line 6 imports HttpTrackingAdapter and line 20 constructs it, which is the wiring the layer rule assigns to the composition root. The use case in application/track.py receives the adapter only through the TrackingPort parameter and never imports it.

TrackingPort is a typing.Protocol defined in the application layer. It is the port the rule requires; application imports domain and ports only, and it imports domain.parcel.Parcel (allowed). The adapter implements the port by method shape, and line 12 of adapters/http_tracking.py subclasses it explicitly, which is the adapter-implements-port direction. A Protocol has no implementation and does not create a dependency on httpx.

Parcel is a frozen dataclass that crosses from adapters/http_tracking.py through the port into application/track.py. It is a value object of the domain layer, so passing it across the boundary is the intended contract and not a leak of adapter types. The domain module imports only the standard library dataclasses module and nothing from application or adapters, so the domain-imports-nothing-outside-domain rule holds.
Literal default base URL in the composition root; the composition root may hold environment defaults.
Adapter-level timeout constant matching the spec; adapters may hold their own transport settings.
